sections.html:
Every operation is one HTTP request to the API's endpoint. A body, in a request or a response, is JSON. The commands here read the endpoint from SURFACE_ENDPOINT:

export SURFACE_ENDPOINT='https://<endpoint>'

Send these headers:

HeaderValueOn
Content-Typeapplication/jsona request with a JSON body
Crucible-Version1every request
x-amz-content-sha256the body's SHA-256, in lowercase hexevery POST, PUT and PATCH (the empty body's digest when there is none) and any other request with a body

Crucible-Version names the release this reference documents. A request without it is served at a release the service chooses, which may be an older one.
sections.markdown:
Every operation is one HTTP request to the API's endpoint. A body, in a request or a response, is JSON. The commands here read the endpoint from `SURFACE_ENDPOINT`:

```sh
export SURFACE_ENDPOINT='https://<endpoint>'
```

Send these headers:

| Header | Value | On |
|---|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | a request with a JSON body |
| `Crucible-Version` | `1` | every request |
| `x-amz-content-sha256` | the body's SHA-256, in lowercase hex | every POST, PUT and PATCH (the empty body's digest when there is none) and any other request with a body |

`Crucible-Version` names the release this reference documents. A request without it is served at a release the service chooses, which may be an older one.
sections.title: Send a request

sections.html:
ListThings is GET /ListThings:

curl "$SURFACE_ENDPOINT"'/ListThings?build=build' \
  -H 'Crucible-Version: 1'

It answers 200 with a JSON body:

{
  "count": 1,
  "info": "info",
  "nextToken": "nextToken"
}

Every operation's page has its request, its response and a command like this one.

sections.html:
Each of the API's simple types is written in JSON like this:

API typeJSON
stringa string
64-bit integer (long)a whole number, every digit written

A structure is an object with a member for each of its members. Leave an optional member out to send nothing for it. In a path, a query string or a header, a value is written as text. A parser that reads every JSON number as a double (JavaScript's JSON.parse) rounds a whole number past 2^53: read a response with one that keeps every digit where a value can be that large.

sections.html: One operation returns its results in pages. A response carries the next page's token (nextToken in the JSON body) when another page follows: send it as the query parameter token in the next request, with the other parameters unchanged, until a response has none. A token is opaque: do not read or build one, and stop if the service returns the same token twice.

sections.html:
use surface_sdk::*;

let client = SurfaceClient::new(runtime::Config::new(std::env::var("SURFACE_ENDPOINT")?));

The service declares no authentication. Methods are async: run them on an async runtime such as Tokio. The client sends Crucible-Version: 1 on every request.
sections.title: Create a client

sections.html:
list_things calls ListThings. Every operation has a method like it.

use surface_sdk::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // The client sends Crucible-Version: 1 on every request.
    let client = SurfaceClient::new(runtime::Config::new(std::env::var("SURFACE_ENDPOINT")?));

    // Sample values generated from the model's types and constraints.
    let input = ListThingsInput::builder()
        .member_build("build")
        .build();

    let output = client.list_things(input).await?;
    println!("{:?}", output.next_token());
    println!("{:?}", output.member_info());
    println!("{:?}", output.count());
    Ok(())
}

sections.html:
Every value is typed. The API's simple types are these in Rust:

API typeRust
stringString
64-bit integer (long)i64

A list is Vec<T> and a map BTreeMap<K, V>, under the API's own name for it where it has one. An optional member is a runtime::Field<T>: Field::Absent leaves it out, Field::Null sends an explicit null, and Field::Value(value) sends a value. A builder's setter takes the value itself, so only a member you set appears in the request.

sections.html:
A paginated operation also has a <operation>_pages method returning a paginator (client.list_things_pages_2(input)): call next_page().await until it returns None; each page is one response.

use surface_sdk::*;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // The client sends Crucible-Version: 1 on every request.
    let client = SurfaceClient::new(runtime::Config::new(std::env::var("SURFACE_ENDPOINT")?));

    // Sample values generated from the model's types and constraints.
    let input = ListThingsInput::builder()
        .member_build("build")
        .build();

    // Each page is one response; the paginator sends `nextToken` for the next.
    let mut pages = client.list_things_pages_2(input);
    while let Some(page) = pages.next_page().await {
        let page = page?;
        println!("{:?}", page);
    }
    Ok(())
}

sections.html: Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. For operations that declare an idempotency token, an unset token is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. runtime::Config::retry(runtime::Retry { .. }) changes the attempt limit (3, the first included) and backoff; runtime::Retry::none() turns retries off.

sections.html:
Every value is typed. The API's simple types are these in TypeScript:

API typeTypeScript
stringstring
64-bit integer (long)bigint

Each named API type is exported under its own name, and a simple one is an alias of the type above (an API string named Id is type Id = string). A list is T[], a map Record<string, V>, and an enum a const object with a type of its values. An optional member is an optional property: leave it out, and pass null only where the API accepts it. A bigint holds the integers a number cannot hold exactly; stringifyJson, exported from the package, serializes values that contain one, which JSON.stringify refuses.

A paginated operation also has a paginate<Operation> method returning an async iterator of pages (for await (const page of client.paginateListThings_2(input))): each page is one response, and it stops when the response carries no next token.

import { SurfaceClient } from "@example/surface";
import type * as models from "@example/surface";

// The client sends Crucible-Version: 1 on every request, and x-amz-content-sha256 (content-sha256) on every POST, PUT and PATCH (the empty body's digest when there is none) and any other request with a body.
const client = new SurfaceClient();

// Sample values generated from the model's types and constraints.
const input: models.ListThingsInput = {
  build: "build",
};

// Each page is one response; the paginator sends `nextToken` for the next.
for await (const page of client.paginateListThings_2(input)) {
  console.log(page);
}

sections.html: Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. For operations that declare an idempotency token, an unset token is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. Set retry: { maxAttempts } in the client configuration to change the attempt limit (3, the first included), or retry: false to turn retries off.
